title: Replying to @liz_doesthings its a very, very well done adaptation and...
transcript: Kimberly Akimbo The Musical is in fact an adaptation of Kimberly Akimbo the play that was also written by David Lindsay-Abaire in the early 2 thousands and I've seen a lot of people try to give Kimberly Akimbo an exception and call it an original work or not wanna call it an adaptation for a variety of different reasons and I would challenge people not to do that because I think when we do that we lose a more interesting conversation surrounding adaptations themselves part of the instinct to wanna call Kimberly akimbo comes from the stereotype that adaptations themselves are inherently bad or like cash grabs and I think Kimberly Akimbo is the perfect example of why they aren't and why we shouldn't just automatically shit on adaptations when they get announced because yes we definitely want to uplift original works original works are just so much harder to sell and that's a whole conversation in itself but adapting art of any medium into a musical is a skill in and of itself and when we give something like Kimberly Akimbo an exception we are ignoring the more fascinating conversation there which is what makes a good adaptation there's also interesting conversations to be had in like the exceptions that people are willing to give Kimberly Akimbo one that I've seen a lot is the fact that David Lindsay-Abaire wrote the original play as well as the book to the musical so of course the idea of Kimberly Akimbo’s story was original to him as a writer but I think that argument kind of ignores the massive amount of skill that both David Lindsay Abaire and Janine Tesori have in being able to adapt an entirely spoken word world and expand it out to include songs and to include an entire chorus of teenagers like that was brilliant also when you look at something like Almost Famous that was based off of a movie that was originally written by Cameron Crowe who ended up writing the book to the musical as well and so even though that idea was original to him that adaptation still has a lot of challenges and going from the film format to the musical format it's also a whole conversation to be had about how a play is originally a 2x structure a film is a 3x structure but a musical is a 2x structure and a lot of movie to musical adaptations struggle in going from the 01:57 act structures but of course that doesn't mean that all movie adaptations are bad there are plenty of really good movie to musical adaptations we also see people give Kimberly akimbo exceptions because it's not based off of a very well known IP there's definitely a conversation to be had there as well about some of the advantages and disadvantages of adapting a well known property versus a not well known property into a musical like of course the challenge of having to find an audience as opposed to having one already built in but with a built in audience you do have to do a level of fan service that a lot of musicals struggle with ultimately I would encourage people to not call Kimberly a Kimbo an original musical because I think it does take away from how good of an adaptation it is and it continues this idea that adaptations are just inherently bad when they're not they're not they're great
